Elected as Toronto's mayor in 2023, this former NDP member of Parliament was previously married to a fellow NDP leader who led the Official Opposition in 2011 — who is she?
Serving as Argentina's Minister of National Security under both Javier Milei and Mauricio Macri, this senator represents Buenos Aires for La Libertad Avanza — who is she?
Known as the 'Bandit Queen,' this Indian outlaw-turned-politician was charged in absentia over a 1981 massacre before later serving as a member of parliament — who is she?
Phoolan Devi: Indian bandit and politician (1963–2001)

Nicknamed 'the Flautist' for his love of playing the flute at Dionysian festivals, this Macedonian-Greek king ruled Egypt twice and was a descendant of one of Alexander the Great's generals — who was he?
Ptolemy XII Auletes: Ptolemaic King of Egypt, 80–51 BC.
Taking office in December 1983, this Argentine lawyer and social democrat was the first democratically elected president after the country's military 'National Reorganization Process' — who was he?
Raúl Alfonsín: President of Argentina from 1983 to 1989.
Deposed in a 2017 coup after ruling Zimbabwe for 37 years as both prime minister and president, who was this revolutionary-turned-leader?
Robert Mugabe: Leader of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 2017.
In 2016, a former care-home employee killed 19 disabled residents in Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan, in the deadliest mass stabbing the country had seen in decades — what is this attack called?
Sagamihara stabbings: 2016 hate crime in Japan.
These horse-mounted nomads swept out of Central Asia to dominate the Pontic Steppe by the 8th century BC, later raiding West Asia after crossing the Caucasus — who were they?
Scythians: Nomadic Iranic people of the Pontic Steppe.
One of Noah's sons in Genesis, this biblical figure is considered an ancestor of Abraham and lent his name to the term for a group of West Asian peoples — who is he?
Shem: Biblical figure, son of Noah. Shem (Hebrew: שֵׁם Šēm; Arabic: سَام, romanized: Sām) is one of the sons of Noah in the Bible (Genesis 5–11 and 1 Chronicles 1:4).
This left-wing ideology is defined by social ownership of the means of production — public, cooperative, or employee-held — rather than private ownership. What is it?
Socialism: Political philosophy emphasising social ownership of production.
It's the season when the earliest sunrises and latest sunsets crowd around a single solstice — and when half the planet swelters, the other half shivers. Which season is it?
Summer: Hottest of the four temperate seasons.
Convicted for conspiring in the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, this Michigan-born man briefly served in the U.S. Army alongside his co-conspirator before their plot together — who is he?
The eighth shogun of his family's shogunate, ruling from 1716 to 1745, this samurai is remembered for repealing Japan's ban on Western literature — who was he?
Tokugawa Yoshimune: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1716 to 1745.
As third caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, this son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad ordered the standardized compilation of the Quran still used today — who was he?
Credited with coining the phrase 'sovereign democracy' while shaping Kremlin strategy for over a decade, this close Putin aide earned the nickname 'grey cardinal' — who is he?
As chief of the OKW, this German field marshal signed the criminal orders that fed countless war crimes — and was so deferential to Hitler that colleagues reviled him. Who was he?
Founded in London in 1844 by George Williams to promote 'muscular Christianity,' this youth organization now serves over 64 million people worldwide?
YMCA: Worldwide youth organization. YMCA is a worldwide youth organization based in Vernier, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland, with more than 64 million beneficiaries in 120 countries.
Emerging in late-19th-century Europe in reaction to antisemitism and led by Theodor Herzl, this nationalist movement sought a Jewish homeland in Palestine — what is it?
Zionism: Jewish nationalist movement. The arrival of Zionist settlers in Palestine during this period is widely seen as marking the start of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these was founded earliest?
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these is a physicist?
John Logie Baird is a physicist. In 1928, the Baird Television Development Company achieved the first transatlantic television transmission.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Ingrid Daubechies is a mathematician. Baroness Ingrid Daubechies ( doh-bə-SHEE; French: [dobʃi]; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
What is the atomic number of Darmstadtium?
Darmstadtium: Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
What is the atomic number of Gold?
Gold: Gold is a chemical element; its chemical symbol is Au (from Latin aurum) and atomic number 79.
In what year was Janet Yellen born?
Janet Yellen: Yellen is the Eugene E. and Catherine M.
In what year was Hippocrates born?
Hippocrates: Hippocrates is also widely recognized for his contributions to medical ethics, being credited with the Hippocratic Oath that remains in use today.
In what year was Zakir Naik born?
Zakir Naik: Zakir Abdul Karim Naik (born 18 October 1965) is an Indian Islamic da'i and orator who focuses on comparative religion.
In what year did Guglielmo Marconi die?
Guglielmo Marconi: In 1929, he was ennobled as a marquess (Italian: marchese) by King Victor Emmanuel III, thus becoming the 1st Marchese di Marconi.
In what year did Ibn Khaldun die?
Ibn Khaldun: Ibn Khaldun (27 May 1332 – 17 March 1406, 732–808 AH) was an Arab scholar, historian, philosopher, and sociologist.
In what year was Phosphorus discovered?
Phosphorus: Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.

Sukhoi Su-57: Komsomolsk-on-Amur Aircraft Production Association. The Sukhoi Su-57 (Russian: Сухой Су-57; NATO reporting name: Felon) is a twin-engine stealth multirole fighter aircraft developed by Sukhoi.
Which country is Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23 from?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet Union. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Who is credited with discovering Pictor?
Pictor: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Pictor is a constellation in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere, located between the star Canopus and the Large Magellanic Cloud.
Who is credited with discovering Proxima Centauri?
Proxima Centauri: Robert T. A. Innes. Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Who is credited with discovering Stirling's approximation?
Stirling's approximation: Abraham de Moivre. In mathematics, Stirling's approximation (or Stirling's formula) is an asymptotic approximation for factorials.
Who is credited with discovering Yttrium?
Yttrium: Johan Gadolin. Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.

The first woman to officially attend a Dutch university, she became one of the Netherlands' earliest female physicians and, in 1882, opened the world's first birth control clinic — who was this suffrage leader?
Aletta Jacobs (Dutch; 9 February 1854 - 10 August 1929) was a Dutch physician and women's suffrage activist.
This order of ray-finned fish is named for a modified fin ray that dangles like bait to lure in prey, much like a human with a fishing rod — what are they called?

Anglerfish are ray-finned fish in the order Lophiiformes. The majority are bottom-dwellers, being demersal fish, while the aberrant deep-sea anglerfish are pelagic, (mostly) living high in the water column.
With almost 500 species in the daisy family, this large plant genus includes mugwort, wormwood, and sagebrush, and is sometimes confused with a related genus of sages — which genus?
Artemisia (plant) (art--) is a large, diverse genus of plants belonging to the daisy family, Asteraceae, with almost 500 species.
Which SI unit of radioactivity honors the scientist who co-discovered the phenomenon alongside the Curies?
Becquerel (symbol: Bq) is the unit of radioactivity in the International System of Units (SI).
In this distributed ledger, each record carries a cryptographic hash of the one before it, so altering any block would mean rewriting every block that follows — what is this technology called?
Blockchain is a distributed ledger with growing lists of records (blocks) that are securely linked together via cryptographic hashes.
This English guard-dog breed combines the size of the Mastiff with genes from the extinct Old English Bulldog, and gained Kennel Club recognition in 1924 — which breed?
Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Mexican business magnate was ranked the richest person in the world by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, building his fortune through a sprawling conglomerate called Grupo Carso. Who is he?
Carlos Slim (born 28 January 1940) is a Mexican business oligarch, investor and philanthropist.

Sold under the brand name Thorazine, this phenothiazine antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder — but it's also been used for nausea, pre-surgery anxiety, and even stubborn hiccups. What is it?
Chlorpromazine (CPZ), marketed under the brand names Thorazine and Largactil among others, is an antipsychotic medication.

This highly venomous, nocturnal snake, black or bluish-black with narrow white crossbands, is widely distributed across South Asia, from grasslands to agricultural fields to human settlements — what snake is it?
Common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.

Named for a mythological Greek youth who was transformed into a tree after accidentally killing a beloved stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is considered polyphyletic by modern genetic analysis — what genus is it?
Cupressus (common name cypress) is one of several genera of evergreen conifers within the family Cupressaceae; for the others, see cypress.
Caused by a Corynebacterium bacterium, this infection can spin a tough grey 'pseudomembrane' across the throat that slowly chokes off the airway — what is it?
Diphtheria is an infection caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae. The pseudomembrane can grow to cover a wide area of the throat, leading to strangulation and death.

This scientific and engineering discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify the flow of electric current, converting between forms like AC to DC. What is the field called?

Electronics is a scientific and engineering discipline that studies and applies the principles of physics to design, create, and operate devices that manipulate electrons and other electrically charged particles.
This sweet-tasting but toxic diol is a workhorse of antifreeze and polyester manufacturing, and astronomers have even detected the molecule in space — what is it?
Ethylene glycol (IUPAC name: ethane-1,2-diol) is an organic compound (a vicinal diol) with the formula (CH2OH)2.

Also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome after the pair of psychiatrists who first described it, this shared delusional disorder is named for the small number of people who typically experience it together — what is it called?

Folie à deux (French for 'madness of two'), also called shared psychosis or shared delusional disorder (SDD), is a rare psychiatric syndrome in which symptoms of a delusional belief are "transmitted" from one individual to another.

A Belgian-British emigrant to New York, this inventor struck gold during a 1906 stay in Central America by perfecting an early instant-coffee process and building a company to mass-produce it — who was he?
George Washington (inventor) (May 20, 1871 - March 29, 1946) was a Belgian-British inventor and businessman.

These common coastal seabirds, most closely related to terns and skimmers, were once known by an older name still surviving in some English dialects and cognate with the German word Möwe — what birds are they?
Gull (see Taxonomy), are seabirds of the subfamily Larinae.
Planted for land reclamation thanks to its nitrogen-fixing, erosion-resisting root system, this deciduous shrub genus's berries also show up in human and animal food products — what genus is it?
Hippophae is a genus of flowering plants in the family Elaeagnaceae.
Prized in folk medicine as an antiseptic and expectorant, this Lamiaceae shrub grows wild from Southern Europe to the Caspian Sea area — which plant is it?
Hyssopus officinalis is a shrub in the Lamiaceae or mint family native to Southern Europe, the Middle East, and the region surrounding the Caspian Sea.
A Scottish surgeon who corrected clubfoot and squints, he's also dubbed by some the 'Father of Modern Hypnotism' — pioneering both hypnotic and chemical anaesthesia. Who was this gentleman scientist?
James Braid (surgeon) (19 June 1795 - 25 March 1860) was a Scottish surgeon, natural philosopher, and "gentleman scientist".

An evergreen conifer in the cypress family, this small tree or shrub boasts the largest geographical range of any woody plant on Earth, spanning the cool temperate Northern Hemisphere — which species?
Juniperus communis is a species of small tree or shrub in the cypress family Cupressaceae.
Which aromatic Mediterranean evergreen tree, prominent in classical Greco-Roman culture and used to season food, can grow up to 20 meters tall with smooth, glossy leaves?
Laurus nobilis is an aromatic evergreen tree or large shrub with green, glabrous (smooth) leaves.
Because its large profile and low operating altitude make it an easy target, this heavily armed gunship variant of the C-130 Hercules usually flies missions at night. What aircraft is it?
Lockheed AC-130 is a heavily armed, long-endurance, ground-attack variant of the C-130 Hercules transport, fixed-wing aircraft.

One of the most colorful mammals alive, this west-central African monkey wears red and blue on both its face and its rump, with the brightest males being the biggest — long mistaken for a baboon, what is it?
Mandrill (Mandrillus sphinx) is a large Old World monkey native to west central Africa.

Patented in 1922 and used to relieve pain, fever, and spasms, this drug's sale is restricted in some countries due to a rare but serious blood-cell side effect discovered in the 1970s — what drug is it?
Metamizole is a painkiller, spasm reliever, and fever reliever drug.
This fast-growing, drought-resistant tree native to northern India earns nicknames like 'drumstick tree' and 'horseradish tree,' and its leaves and seed pods are eaten as vegetables. What is it?
Moringa oleifera is a short-lived, fast-growing, drought-resistant tree of the family Moringaceae, native to northern India and used extensively in South and Southeast Asia.

Encompassing three distinct genetic conditions marked by nervous-system tumors, one type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis while another causes early-onset hearing loss and cataracts — which condition?
Neurofibromatosis (NF) refers to a group of three distinct genetic conditions in which tumors grow in the nervous system.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Taking place over 24 hours at a large investment bank, this drama follows employees navigating the earliest hours of the 2008 financial crisis. What film is it?
Passerine is any bird of the order Passeriformes (from Latin passer 'sparrow' and formis '-shaped'), which includes more than half of all bird species.

Left untreated, this inherited metabolic disorder — caused by a faulty gene needed to break down a certain amino acid — can cause intellectual disability, seizures, and a musty body odor — what is it?
Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
Revered as the 'Father of the Nation,' this Emirati statesman served as the founding president of a Gulf federation from its 1971 independence until his death in 2004. Who is he?
Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
Split into roughly a dozen Afrotropical species and around 167 Neotropical species — among them the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which bird family is this?
Psittacidae is one of three families of true parrots.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging between 6 and 18 months of age, this genetic disorder, caused mainly by mutations in the MECP2 gene, brings repetitive movements, slowed growth, and language impairment — which condition?
Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6-18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.

These lizard-like amphibians, grouped in the order Urodela, keep a tail throughout both their larval and adult life stages — unlike their tailless amphibian cousins the frogs and toads. What animal is it?

Salamander are a group of amphibians typically characterized by their lizard-like appearance, with slender bodies, blunt snouts, short limbs projecting at right angles to the body, and the presence of a tail in both larvae and adults.

Triggered by certain serotonergic medications, this group of symptoms can range from mild high blood pressure to severe, potentially fatal spikes in body temperature and dangerous muscle breakdown — what's it called?
Serotonin syndrome (SS) consists of a group of symptoms that may occur with the use of certain serotonergic medications or drugs.
Known in Hispanic America as guanábana and easily killed by a touch of frost, which Annona fruit blends flavors of strawberry, apple, and sour citrus?
Soursop (also called graviola, guyabano, and in Hispanic America guanbana) is the fruit of Annona muricata, a broadleaf, flowering, evergreen tree.
First flown in 1967 with its crew sitting side by side under variable-sweep wings, this Soviet bomber earned the NATO codename 'Fencer' — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-24 (NATO reporting name: Fencer) is a supersonic, all-weather tactical bomber developed in the Soviet Union.

This mass of gray matter forming part of the forebrain relays sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex through radiating nerve fibers, and helps regulate consciousness, sleep, and alertness — what's the structure?
Thalamus (pl.: thalami; from Greek, "chamber") is a large mass of gray matter on the lateral wall of the third ventricle forming the dorsal part of the diencephalon (a division of the forebrain).
Usually caused by mutations in the TCOF1 gene, which autosomal dominant condition affects facial bone and ear development but not intelligence?
Treacher Collins syndrome (TCS) is a genetic disorder characterized by deformities of the ears, eyes, cheekbones, and chin.
Once classified in the honeysuckle family before molecular studies gave it its own, this genus of 150-plus shrub species reaches Africa only via the Atlas Mountains — which genus?
Viburnum is a genus of about 150-175 species of flowering plants in the family Viburnaceae.
Marketed under names like Rompun, this veterinary sedative and alpha-2 adrenergic agonist is often combined with ketamine for animal anesthesia and used as an emetic in cats — what is it?

Xylazine is a structural analog of clonidine and an 2-adrenergic receptor agonist, sold under many trade names worldwide, most notably the Bayer brand name Rompun, as well as Anased, Sedazine and Chanazine.
Known by the common name yarrow, this pungent, fernleaved plant in the daisy family is used in traditional medicine and as livestock feed — what is its scientific name?
Achillea millefolium: Species of plant. Achillea millefolium, commonly known as yarrow or common yarrow, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.
A former IMF economist, this politician has served as President of Ivory Coast since 2010 after earlier stints as the country's prime minister in the early 1990s — who is he?
Alassane Ouattara: President of Ivory Coast since 2010. Ouattara became the president of the Rally of the Republicans (RDR), an Ivorian political party, in 1999.
Native to the Americas, this plant is better known by its common names common ragweed, annual ragweed, or low ragweed — what is its scientific name?
Ambrosia artemisiifolia: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family.
Brought to Asia by Spanish traders aboard the Manila galleons, this tropical American tree produces a knobby, sweet fruit known as sugar apple or custard apple — what is this plant?
Annona squamosa: Species of tree. Annona squamosa is a small, well-branched tree or shrub from the family Annonaceae that bears edible fruits called sugar apples or sweetsops or custard apples.
This pigmented ring of skin around the nipple contains sebaceous glands as well as the openings of the milk ducts — what's it called?
Areola: Pigmented area on the breast around the nipple.
Developed to herd livestock across rough terrain by nipping at their heels, this short-coated working breed's coat reads as either 'red' or 'blue' — which breed?

Australian Cattle Dog: Breed of herding dog. The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.

This relationship, expressed as A = εcl, links how much light a solution absorbs directly to its concentration — what is this principle called, named after two scientists whose work dates back to the mid-18th century?
Beer–Lambert law: Scientific law describing absorption of light.
Not a species of its own, it's really a melanistic leopard or jaguar whose rosettes are still hidden under the dark coat — what do we call this big-cat colour variant?
Black panther: Variant of leopard and jaguar. Black panthers of both species have excess black pigments, but their typical rosettes are also present.
This subfamily of horned, cloven-hooved ungulates includes cattle, bison, and both African and water buffalo, with the gaur as its largest living member — which group?
In 1930, which Indian physicist won the Nobel Prize for discovering that light changes wavelength when passing through a transparent material, becoming the first Asian to win a Physics Nobel?

Defined by a –COOH functional group attached to an R-group, and only partially dissociating in water, this general class of organic compounds includes fatty compounds and the building blocks of proteins — what is this functional class called?
Carboxylic acid: Organic compound containing a –C(=O)OH group.
Often called the Judas tree, this small deciduous redbud native to Southern Europe and Western Asia bursts into deep pink blossoms each spring — what species is it?

Caused by a bacterium spread through contaminated water and undercooked shellfish, this intestinal infection produces severe watery diarrhea that can trigger dehydration within hours — which disease is it?
Cholera: Bacterial infection of the small intestine.
Commonly called the tailbone, this bone is the vestigial remnant of a tail in humans and other tailless primates, sitting just below the sacrum — which bone?
Coccyx: Bone of the pelvis. In tailless primates (e.g. humans and other great apes) since Nacholapithecus (a Miocene hominoid), the coccyx is the remnant of a vestigial tail.
One of the few metals found in nature in directly usable metallic form, this soft, pinkish-orange element with symbol Cu prizes its high thermal and electrical conductivity — what is it?
Copper: Chemical element with atomic number 29 (Cu)
Caused by prolonged exposure to excess cortisol, this condition produces abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and reddish stretch marks — which condition is it?
Cushing's syndrome: Symptoms from excessive exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

Known mainly through DNA evidence rather than plentiful fossils, this extinct archaic human group ranged across Asia until about 32,000 years ago, and DNA analysis confirmed the Harbin skull belonged to it — what group is it?
Denisovan: Archaic human species from Asia.
In 1949, this NASA mathematician became the first African-American woman to supervise a team at Langley, later teaching herself and her staff the Fortran language — who is she?
Dorothy Vaughan: American human computer and computer programmer (1910–2008)
Known as aubergine or brinjal elsewhere, this purple, spongy fruit in the nightshade family is technically a berry despite usually being cooked as a vegetable — what is it?
A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime, this social psychologist and democratic socialist helped found a psychoanalytic institute in New York and was linked to the Frankfurt School — who is he?
Once widespread during the Pleistocene and later reintroduced by humans to its ancient range, which hoofed mammal species is native to Turkey and possibly Italy, the Balkans, and Rhodes?
European fallow deer: Species of hooved mammal. The European fallow deer (Dama dama), also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
This genus of about 850 tropical tree, shrub, and vine species is best known for two cultivated fruit-bearing members and serves as a vital food source for wildlife across the tropics — which genus?
Ficus: Genus of flowering plants in the mulberry family Moraceae.
Native from the British Isles east to the Caucasus, this tree in the olive family is prized for wood that's flexible, strong, and lightweight — what is its scientific name?
Fraxinus excelsior: Species of deciduous tree.
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?
This type of organ produces an organism's sex hormones and gametes — testicles in males, ovaries in females — what is it called?
Gonad: Gland that produces sex cells.
This standard markup language structures web documents using elements delineated by tags, often paired with CSS and JavaScript — what is it?
HTML: Markup language for documents. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
The only Saskatchewan-born Nobel laureate, this Canadian-born chemist won the 1983 prize for unraveling the mechanisms of electron-transfer reactions in metal complexes — who was he?

Galaxies recede from Earth at speeds proportional to their distance, a relationship credited to a 1929 paper — though the maths behind an expanding universe had already been derived in 1922 by Alexander Friedmann. What's this relationship called?
Hubble's law: Observation in physical cosmology.
This 14th-century Arab scholar wrote his most famous work, the Muqaddimah, in just six months and once met the conqueror Tamerlane — who is he?
Ibn Khaldun: Arab Islamic scholar, historian and philosopher (1332–1406)
This Russian physiologist won the 1904 Nobel Prize for his work on digestion, but is far better remembered for training dogs to salivate at a signal — who was he?
Once an assistant to astronomer Tycho Brahe and later imperial mathematician to Emperor Rudolf II, this polymath formulated the laws of planetary motion — who was he?
Johannes Kepler: German astronomer and mathematician (1571–1630)

A NASA mathematician and human computer, she calculated the orbital mechanics critical to America's first crewed spaceflights and was among the first African-American women to work as a NASA scientist — who was she?
This inflammation of the voice box causes symptoms ranging from a hoarse voice to complete voice loss, typically clearing up within two weeks — what is the condition?
Laryngitis: Inflammation of the larynx (voice box). The primary symptom is loss of some vocal function, ranging from hoarse voice to no voice at all.
Syntax, semantics, morphology, phonetics, phonology, and pragmatics are all branches of which scientific field?

This fibrous gourd, edible only when picked young, becomes a scrubbing sponge once fully ripened — and one grown in Graham, NC, broke the world heaviest record in October 2025 at 11 lb 3.3 oz. What is it?
Native to the Malay Peninsula and Borneo, this tropical fruit hides sweet, tangy white flesh beneath a deep reddish-purple rind — which fruit?
Mangosteen: Tropical evergreen tree with edible fruit.
Combined with formaldehyde to create hardwearing resins found in Formica countertops, plastic dinnerware, and the foam in a Magic Eraser, this nitrogen-rich compound also resists fire — what is it?
Melamine: Fire-resistant chemical used in dinnerware, insulation, and cleaning products.
North of the Arctic Circle in summer, this phenomenon keeps the sky lit long after the clock strikes twelve — what is it called?
Midnight sun: Natural phenomenon when daylight lasts for a whole day.
This rounded mound of fatty tissue overlies the junction where the two pubic bones meet — what is it?
Mons pubis: Rounded mass of fatty tissue found over the pubic symphysis.

Dropped from a B-52 and boosted by a modified Pegasus rocket stage before its own scramjet took over, this experimental hypersonic craft still holds the record for fastest jet-powered flight at about Mach 9.6 — what is it?
NASA X-43: Unmanned US experimental hypersonic aircraft, 1991-2000.

Named for a mythological daughter of Tantalus, this silvery transition metal with atomic number 41 was once called columbium and is now prized as a nickel-free option in hypoallergenic jewelry — which element?
Niobium: Chemical element with atomic number 41 (Nb)
This British engineer rewrote Maxwell's equations into the form we use today and devised the telegrapher's equations — who was he?
Oliver Heaviside: British mathematician and electrical engineer (1850–1925)

Though isolated observations date back to the 6th century BC, this science's modern foundation is credited to Georges Cuvier's 1796 work demonstrating that species could go extinct — what field is this?
Paleontology: Study of past life through fossils.
This thick, fan-shaped muscle underlies the breast and is responsible for flexing, adducting, and internally rotating the upper arm — which chest muscle?
Pectoralis major: Main human chest muscle.

First described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the "cellar spider" and "vibrating spider" — and shares a famous leggy nickname with harvestmen and crane flies. What family is it?
Pholcidae: Family of spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.
This inflammatory lung condition attacks the tiny air sacs called alveoli, usually after a viral or bacterial infection, and often shows up on a chest X-ray — what is it?
Pneumonia: Inflammation of the alveoli of the lungs.
Discovered in 1857 by French chemist Marcellin Berthelot, this three-carbon alkane turns liquid under pressure and now fuels countless backyard barbecues — what gas is it?
A group of these mid-sized Galliformes birds is called a covey or bevy, and 40 million of them were farm-raised in the US back in 2007 alone — what bird is it?
Quail: Index of animals with the same common name.

Also known as Willis–Ekbom disease, this neurological disorder creates an overwhelming urge to move one's limbs, especially when at rest, often described as a crawling or tingling sensation — what's the condition called?
Restless legs syndrome: Medical condition. There is often an unpleasant feeling in the legs that improves temporarily by moving them.
Also known as sixth disease, this childhood viral infection typically strikes before age three with a sudden fever followed by a pink rash lasting under three days — what's the condition called?
Roseola: Human disease caused by human herpesviruses.
This Indian-American executive became CEO of a major tech company in 2014, succeeding Steve Ballmer, after leading its cloud and enterprise division — who is he?
In this biological process, haploid gametes such as sperm and egg cells combine to form a zygote that develops into a diploid organism — what is it called?
Sexual reproduction: Biological process. Sexual reproduction is the most common life cycle in multicellular eukaryotes, such as animals, fungi and plants.
